recorded_issue_verbatim.issue: AC-015's ordering criterion is not actually tested. `test/implement-contract.test.ts:449` asserts `/after[^.]{0,40}commit/` against the entire lowercased COMMIT step, and that regex is already satisfied by pre-existing step-6 prose at `workflows/forge-implement.js:1796` ("…on the staged files LAST (after any lint --fix); commit WITHOUT --no-verify…"), independently of step 7. Proven by mutation: replacing `workflows/forge-implement.js:1800` "immediately AFTER the commit exists (a sha cannot be written inside the commit it names)" with "as the FIRST thing you do, before you make the checkpoint at all" — the exact inversion AC-015 exists to forbid — leaves both AC-015 tests GREEN (`vitest run test/implement-contract.test.ts -t "AC-015"` → 2 passed). The AC's verification column demands "the same assertion reads the ordering words out of the prompt"; it does not. Compounding this, the implementation report's TDD row (`implementation-report.md:43`) presents this as "RED pre-fix … the ordering words did not exist", crediting the assertion with a discrimination it lacks — the same near-tautology class the author correctly tightened for AC-018 in review #2.
